title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Jamie Chen
body:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures covering: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and a set of canonical internal templates. The goal is a single, authoritative reference for employees and managers to follow consistent, auditable processes.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems and data.
- Exclusions: team-local operational runbooks and legal-contract terms (see finance-and-legal).

Ownership and maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (policy steward).
- Day-to-day operational owners: Security (access control), Eng SRE (change management), Finance (procurement/expenses), Legal (vendor contracts).
- Review cadence: annual full review; ad hoc updates for regulatory or operational changes.

1) Access & permissions (RBAC and onboarding/offboarding)

Purpose: grant least-privilege, auditable access and timely deprovisioning.

Key principles
- Least privilege: grant the minimum permissions necessary for job function.
- Approval: manager + system owner approval required for elevated access.
- Timeboxed access: temporary elevated access with an expiration (default 7 days).
- Auditability: all changes must be tracked in the access management system (IAM logs).

Standard process (new access request)
1. Employee or manager submits an access request using the Access Request template via the Access Portal (okta.redwood.com/access-requests).
2. Request routes to the requester's manager for business justification.
3. System owner reviews for technical scope and approves or denies.
4. Security performs automated policy check (conflict of interest, sensitive data scope).
5. On approval, IAM automation provisions access and emails the requester + manager; entry recorded in audit log.
6. Automated expiration: temporary grants auto-revoke on expiry; permanent grants require annual recertification.

Service accounts and API keys
- Service accounts must be named by team prefix (e.g., eng-ci-build), have an owner, and use vault-managed secrets.
- API keys and long-lived credentials are prohibited in code or public repos; rotate every 90 days or sooner if exposed.

Emergency access (break-glass)
- Break-glass requests must be raised through Oncall and notify Security and the manager immediately.
- All break-glass sessions are logged and reviewed by Security within 48 hours.

SLA and metrics
- Standard access requests: target 3 business days for completion.
- Elevated access requests: target 1 business day.
- Offboarding: revoke access within 24 hours of termination notification.

2) Change management (platform & infra changes)

Purpose: ensure safe, auditable, and low-risk changes to production services and infra.

Change types
- Minor change: documented configuration updates with no expected customer impact.
- Standard change: routine changes with a known rollback and pre-approved CAB policy.
- Major change: architectural or customer-facing changes requiring full change request and CAB review.

Procedure
1. Create a Change Request in the Change Tracker (Jira project: CHG). Include description, rollback plan, test plan, blast radius, owners, and scheduled window.
2. For Standard and Major changes, attach automated test artifacts and performance impact estimates.
3. CAB review: Standard changes reviewed in weekly CAB or via asynchronous approvals for low-risk items; Major changes require an engineering review meeting.
4. Pre-deploy: run testing in staging and canary if applicable.
5. Deploy during scheduled window; monitor defined health checks for the first two hours.
6. Post-deploy: fill change completion form and mark CR resolved.
7. Post-incident: if the change caused a disruption, open an incident review and link to the CR.

Emergency changes
- Label CR as EMERGENCY and notify SRE and Security. An after-action review is required within 72 hours.

Required fields for every CR
- Summary: short description
- Owner: primary engineer
- Business/Customer impact: low/medium/high
- Rollback plan: step-by-step
- Test plan: automated + manual checks
- Monitoring: metric thresholds and alarms
- Communication plan: stakeholders and status page update owner

3) Data management (classification, handling, retention)

Data classification levels
- Public: content safe for public consumption.
- Internal: internal company information, low risk.
- Confidential: business-sensitive (e.g., pricing, roadmaps).
- Restricted: regulated or customer-sensitive data (PII, PCI, PHI).

Handling rules by classification
- Access: map to RBAC roles; Restricted data requires explicit owner approval and encryption at rest & in transit.
- Storage: restricted data must reside in approved storage (encrypted S3 or on-prem vault).
- Transmission: use TLS 1.2+; avoid sending restricted data over email without DLP.
- Logging: redact sensitive fields in application logs; use structured logging with tokenized identifiers.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: 3 years for Internal/Confidential data unless otherwise specified.
- Restricted data: follow contractual and regulatory retention schedules; automate deletion where possible.
- Data deletion requests: follow Data Subject Request procedure; contact Legal and Security.

Data transfers and residency
- Cross-border transfer of Restricted data requires Legal approval and review of adequacy.
- Use company-approved partners for data processing.

Data incident response
- Any suspected data exfiltration must be escalated to Security within 1 hour.
- Follow the Security incident response runbook and notify Legal for breach evaluation.

4) Procurement and expenses

Principles
- Spend with ROI and compliance in mind.
- Use preferred vendors and procurement channels where possible.
- All purchases require manager approval; purchases > $25k require Finance and Legal approval.

Procurement workflow
1. Requestor fills the Purchase Request form and attaches justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2. Manager approves in the procurement system.
3. For hardware or contracts > $5k, Procurement/Finance reviews vendor terms and issues PO.
4. Finance issues payment and ensures proper GL coding.

Expense reimbursement
- Employees should submit expense reports within 30 days of the expense.
- Receipts are required for any expense > $25.
- Travel expenses follow the Travel policy.

Approval matrix
- Up to $1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,001-25,000: Manager + Finance review.
- > $25,000: Manager + Finance + Legal approval and Exec sponsor.

5) Vendor management and third-party risk

Goals: manage vendor lifecycle from onboarding to offboarding while controlling security, compliance, and commercial risk.

Vendor lifecycle steps
1. Pre-onboarding: Risk assessment (security questionnaire + financial vetting).
2. Contracting: Legal reviews terms; include data protection addenda when required.
3. Onboarding: assign vendor owner, set least-privilege access, and add to Vendor Registry.
4. Monitoring: periodic security reviews, SLA performance checks, and invoices reconciliation.
5. Offboarding: revoke access, collect assets, and retain contract records per retention schedule.

Vendor risk matrix
- Low risk: non-critical SaaS tools with no customer data. Annual review.
- Medium risk: tools with internal data or moderate access. Quarterly review.
- High risk: vendors processing Restricted data or core infrastructure. Continuous monitoring and contractual security requirements.

Required contract clauses
- Data protection and breach notification timelines (<= 72 hours).
- Right to audit (for high-risk vendors).
- Subprocessor disclosure and approval.

6) Travel policy (business travel and reimbursements)

Booking and approvals
- All business travel must be pre-approved by the manager. Use the corporate travel portal to book flights and hotels.
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours; premium economy for flights 6-10 hours; exec approval required for > 10 hours.

Per diem and allowable expenses
- Meals: actuals up to policy limits by region; receipts required.
- Ground transportation: rideshares or standard rental cars; rental car insurance covered if using vendor partners.
- Lodging: use recommended hotels where available; exceptions require manager justification.

Expense submission
- Submit travel expenses within 14 days of return with receipts and itinerary.
- Non-compliant claims may be rejected and require resubmission.

Safety and conduct
- Follow local laws and Redwood code of conduct. For international travel, consult Security and TravelOps for higher-risk locations.

7) Internal templates (canonical forms and examples)

Access Request template (use in Access Portal)
Title: [Short description of access required]
Requester: [Name & email]
Manager: [Name & email]
System: [service name or data store]
Role/Permissions requested: [list]
Business justification: [why access is required]
Requested duration: [temporary/permanent] - if temporary, end date
System owner: [Name & email]

Purchase Request template (Procurement system)
Title: [Short description of purchase]
Requestor: [Name & email]
Manager: [Name & email]
Vendor: [name & URL]
Estimated cost: [currency amount]
Budget code: [GL code]
Justification: [business need]
Contract required: [yes/no]
Attachment: [quote/requirements]

Change Request minimal checklist (use CHG Jira)
Summary: [one-line]
Owner: [engineer name]
Risk: [low/med/high]
Rollback steps: [numbered steps]
Monitoring: [metrics & dashboards]
Schedule window: [date/time]

Data deletion request (DSR) minimal fields
Subject: [user id/email or data subject identifier]
Scope: [systems/data locations]
Requested by: [name/email]
Deadline: [date]

8) Exceptions, enforcement, and escalation

Exceptions
- Exceptions to these policies must be requested via the Policy Exception form and approved by People Ops + the owning function. All exceptions are timeboxed and recorded.

Enforcement
- Non-compliance may lead to access revocation, expense denial, or disciplinary action depending on severity.

Escalation path
1. Primary owner (policy/function owner).
2. People Ops.
3. Security or Finance (as relevant).
4. CEO / Exec sponsor for unresolved high-impact exceptions.

Questions and feedback
For questions about interpretation or to request templates integrated into your team workspace, contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com) or file a request in the People Ops queue.
